raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Split Kimi-K3 quantization by Ascend hardware and generate the documented A5 PD deployment instead of the generic NIXL layout.

- A3 selects only W4A8 (Ascend), using ModelScope `Eco-Tech/Kimi-K3-w4a8`. A5 selects only MXFP4(ASCEND), using the contributor-confirmed private ModelScope checkpoint `Eco-Tech/Kimi-K3-w4a8-mxfp-quarot`. FP8 remains restricted to NVIDIA/AMD.
- A5 PD requires `MooncakeConnectorV2`: each P instance is **DP1/TP8/PP4/EP8**, each D instance is **DP4/TP8/EP32**. Each instance occupies four nodes with eight NPUs per node. Default 1P1D uses eight nodes / 64 NPUs; each pool grows in complete independent 32-NPU groups.
- Mixed serving explicitly declares `worker_args: ["--headless"]` in both A3/A5 strategy hardware overrides: node 0 retains the API, and workers 1–3 join headlessly with their respective DP ranks. The guide records these roles.
- Add the official role arguments/environment and DSpark P eager=true / D eager=false settings. The companion renderer supplies the Ascend proxy, group ranks/masters and guarded UI/API choices.
- The inherited 1711 GB loading estimate remains explicitly unverified for the private A5 checkpoint.

- A5 PD exposes **Scripts → Prefill → Decode → Start_Server → Start_Proxy**. Scripts downloads only `launch_online_dp.py`. Prefill/Decode save `run_dp_template.sh`, with manual `<NIC_NAME>` / `<LOCAL_IP>` edits on each node. Start_Server supplies separate Prefill and Decode launcher commands with rank/master/port arguments and individual copy buttons; no role-selection wrapper is needed. The independent installed proxy starts in step five. The templates follow [official section 5.2](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/blob/main/docs/source/tutorials/models/Kimi-K3.md#52-basic-eight-node-pd-separation-deployment), retaining the required K3 model selection and PP4/DP4 topology.

Reference: [official basic eight-node PD deployment](https://docs.vllm.ai/projects/vllm-ascend-cn/zh-cn/latest/tutorials/models/Kimi-K3.html#52-basic-eight-node-pd-separation-deployment).

Companions: https://github.com/vllm-project/recipes/pull/1152 and https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/19703. Merge the renderer support first; the validation workflow temporarily pins its PR ref. The current source-PR preview renderer on main cannot render the new fields until then. This extends existing PRs and avoids duplicate work; the renderer branch includes pending overlay infrastructure from recipes#1160.

- Kimi-K3 Ascend 910C (A3) and 950DT (A5) support **KV Offload = Off only**, for mixed and PD serving. A hardware-scoped recipe policy disables all other options and normalizes stale URL/saved selections to Off; command synthesis independently ignores offload requests on those profiles.

The KV-offload restriction and nested-connector follow-up were not tested, at the user's request.

- Ascend `--headless` is confined to mixed TP+DP worker nodes. PD Prefill and Decode omit it on every rank, in generated templates and direct commands; the PD UI and guide use the same distinction. This correction follows the contributor's deployment requirement.

This headless correction has not been tested, at the user's request. Existing test expectations were updated without execution.

Earlier validation (completed before this follow-up):
- Strict merged assembly and JSON API build passed: 217 models, 279 promoted variants.
- Connector/overlay/preset regressions: 63/63, including source-driven mixed worker arguments, head/PD isolation and overlay scope.
- Schema, exclusive variants, hardware-switch fallback and core/overlay cutover checks passed.
- Compared 480 existing NVIDIA/AMD configurations against the previous renderer/source: generated commands, arguments and environment are unchanged.
- Local UI confirms manual template network values, independently copyable Prefill/Decode Start_Server commands, all five tabs, fixed topology, Mooncake V2 / Ascend Router / Python, and complete four-node groups.
- The official `launch_online_dp.py` was executed with generated role templates and mock vLLM for P/D group heads and replicated-group followers: **4/4**. Manual NIC/IP values, JSON KV/draft bindings, rank/master parameters and headless roles passed. No NPU process was started.
- `git diff --check` passed. Pre-commit is unavailable here. No NPU inference, accuracy or performance evaluation was run; the private MXFP4 checkpoint and replicated groups remain hardware-unverified.

AI assistance: Codex prepared the configuration, renderer changes and static validation. Human review and hardware verification remain required before merge.

   - **Prefix-match unit**: K3 is a hybrid model: its MLA attention layers and KDA (Mamba-like) layers form two KV-cache groups under the hybrid KV-cache manager. With prefix caching on, vLLM pads the attention block size up to match the Mamba state page, so both groups resolve to one (large) block size and the default prefix-cache hit boundary lands on that block — very coarse. The Blackwell profile sets `--prefix-match-unit 128`: the inflation formula always yields a multiple of 128, so 128 divides whatever block size results, and it aligns with the MLA kernel's native block boundary, giving finer prefix-hit granularity. The value is only effective when prefix caching (or a KV connector) is active; it is a no-op otherwise, and it is safe under all tensor-parallel layouts.
   - **Decode context parallelism (DCP)**: the qualified DCP layouts are part of the presets that ran them: DCP8 on the GB200 aggregated TP8 x PP2 and GB300 disaggregated TP8 pools, DCP16 on the GB200 TP16 disaggregated pools, DCP16/DCP8 at the GB300 low-latency points, and DCP8 in the MI355X AgentX cells. Each pairs `--decode-context-parallel-size` (a divisor of the tensor-parallel size) with `--dcp-comm-backend a2a` and an MLA attention backend that supports it (`TOKENSPEED_MLA` with `mla_prefill_backend: TRTLLM_RAGGED` on Blackwell, `ROCM_AITER_MLA` with `mla_prefill_backend: ROCM_AITER_FA` on MI355X). On builds that carry them, the `VLLM_USE_DIRECT_DCP_A2A`, `VLLM_USE_DIRECT_DCP_Q_GATHER` and `VLLM_USE_DIRECT_DCP_KV_GATHER` knobs default to auto; set them to `1` to pin the direct DCP ops or `0` to disable them, as the MI355X cells do.
   - Ascend W4A8 checkpoint (ModelScope): https://www.modelscope.cn/models/Eco-Tech/Kimi-K3-w4a8
+  - Ascend MXFP4 QuaRot checkpoint (ModelScope): https://www.modelscope.cn/models/Eco-Tech/Kimi-K3-w4a8-mxfp-quarot
   - vLLM Ascend tutorial: https://docs.vllm.ai/projects/ascend/en/v0.23.0/tutorials/models/Kimi-K3.html
 
   ## AMD MI355X: disaggregated prefill and decode
@@ -1661,3 +1872,51 @@ guide: |
   ```
 
   Confirm that a final answer is returned, and inspect the prefill/decode logs for successful KV transfers and transfer errors. Health checks alone do not exercise RDMA. Preserve `reasoning_content` and tool calls when building multi-turn conversations, as described in the [model card](https://huggingface.co/moonshotai/Kimi-K3#6-model-usage).
+
+  ## Ascend mixed Prefill/Decode deployment
+
+  KV Offload supports only **Off** on Ascend 910C (A3) and 950DT (A5), in both
+  mixed and disaggregated serving. Simple, CPU offloading, Mooncake Store, and
+  LMCache are unavailable for these recipe profiles.
+
+  In the four-node A3/A5 mixed deployment, node 0 runs the API server and
+  Nodes 1-3 join with `--headless` and their respective
+  `--data-parallel-start-rank` values of 1, 2, and 3.
+  Follow the [official mixed deployment reference](https://docs.vllm.ai/projects/vllm-ascend-cn/zh-cn/latest/tutorials/models/Kimi-K3.html#51-prefilldecode)
+  for the per-node communication settings and startup order.
+
+  ## Ascend 950DT PD separation
+
+  The A5 PD profile uses MooncakeConnectorV2 and the Ascend load-balancing proxy.
+  Each prefill instance occupies four eight-NPU nodes (DP1/TP8/PP4/EP8), and each
+  decode instance occupies four eight-NPU nodes (DP4/TP8/EP32). Each pool therefore
+  grows in 32-NPU groups; the default is one prefill group plus one decode group
+  (eight nodes, 64 NPUs total). Additional groups are independent replicas.
+
+  The A5 PD builder presents five launch steps:
+
+  1. **Scripts** downloads only `launch_online_dp.py` into the current directory.
+  2. **Prefill** saves `run_dp_template.sh` on each prefill node with TP8/PP4.
+     Manually replace `<NIC_NAME>` and `<LOCAL_IP>` in the template with this
+     node's communication interface and IP.
+  3. **Decode** saves its DP4/TP8 `run_dp_template.sh` on each decode node;
+     manually replace the same two placeholders with that node's values.
+  4. **Start_Server** provides separate Prefill and Decode launcher commands,
+     each with DP/TP size, group-local rank, master address, RPC port, and HTTP
+     port. Run only the matching command on each node. The launcher supplies
+     the template's seven positional arguments. Repeat on all four group nodes.
+  5. **Start_Proxy** starts the client-facing proxy after both pools are ready.
+
+  Run these commands in the installed vLLM Ascend environment. Keep the launcher
+  and the node's own role template in the same directory; do not write both
+  templates on the same node. Container setup belongs to the installation step.
+  Start each prefill group's rank 0 before ranks 1-3. Both Prefill and Decode
+  omit `--headless` in PD separation; only mixed deployment workers use it.
+  Every decode node keeps its HTTP endpoint. The transfer connector remains MooncakeConnectorV2.
+  The launcher runs in the foreground; open another shell for Start_Proxy, which
+  runs the separate proxy script from the vLLM Ascend installation.
+
+  The [official basic PD reference](https://docs.vllm.ai/projects/vllm-ascend-cn/zh-cn/latest/tutorials/models/Kimi-K3.html#52-basic-eight-node-pd-separation-deployment) documents the fixed eight-node
+  topology. Group replication and the private MXFP4 checkpoint have not been
+  validated on NPU hardware here. The guide's pooled PD section adds a MemCache
+  KV cache pool; this profile uses the basic Mooncake V2 transfer path.
